Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Gameplay 3.1 Placing a Meeple 3.2 Resolving a Room 3.2.1 1. Roll for Ghosts 3.2.2 2. Take Cursed Cards 3.2.3 3. Reveal a New Room 4 Game end 4.1 1. Trigger Cursed Cards with Game End Effects 4.2 2. Ghosts 4.3 3. Winner 5 Cursed cards 5.1 Amulet 5.2 Cat 5.3 Clocks 5.4 Doll 5.5 Holy Water 5.6 Mask 5.7 Mirror 5.8 Music Box 5.9 Portrait 5.10 Ring 5.11 Tome 5.12 Twin 6 Rooms 6.1 Attic 6.2 Basement 6.3 Hallway 6.4 Library 6.5 Nursery 6.6 Secret Passage Overview The player with the FEWEST Curses win. During the game, you will acquire Cursed cards that will have a Curse value. Try to collect cards with fewer Curses on them and dispel cards with lots of curses. When you dispel a a card it flips over and its Curses no longer add to your total. Sometimes you'll get haunted by Ghosts. Having a few ghost tokens is okay. But if you end with the MOST ghosts you will gain a lot of Curses. Flashlights protect you from Ghosts. It's risky going further into the haunted house, but you can get 1st choice of the cards. Setup There are multiple Cursed card types but not all will be used each game. At the beginning of the game, several Cursed card types will be selected (5/6/7/8 different types for 2/3/4/5 players). Cards are then shuffled and some are randomly removed (16/12/8/4 removed cards for 2/3/4/5 players). Gameplay On your turn you must place one of your Meeples into a Room. If it is the 3rd Meeple in the Room then the Room will be resolved. Placing a Meeple Place 1 Meeple from your supply on an unoccupied space in any Room. Each placed Meeple will allow to claim one of the cards above the Room. A Meeple placed further up has a better chance of getting 1st choice of cards, but an increased chance of taking Ghosts tokens. Some Rooms have an effect that will activate immediately after placing a Meeple into them. If you place the 3rd Meeple the Room is immediately resolved. Otherwise play passes to the next player. Resolving a Room 1. Roll for Ghosts Roll a number dice equal to the total of the dice symbols on all cards above the Room board. The owner of each Meeple takes Ghosts tokens equal to the number of Ghosts rolled minus the number of Flashlights on the Meeple's space. 2. Take Cursed Cards Beginning with the Meeple in the highest space in the room and continuing down, the owner of the Meeple must take a Cursed card of their choice and adds it to a face-up tableau. Some cards will trigger an effect immediately after claiming them. 3. Reveal a New Room Once all Meeples have claimed cards, the Room is flipped to its opposite side and 3 new cards are dealt to the Room. If no cards remain in the deck, the Room board is removed from the game. Play continues with the next player after the player whose Meeple triggered Room resolution. Once every card has been claimed and all 3 Rooms have been removed from play the game ends. Game end The game ends when all Cursed cards have been taken. Once game end is triggered, the following steps are resolved. 1. Trigger Cursed Cards with Game End Effects All players trigger the end game effects of all end game Cursed cards visible in their tableau. 2. Ghosts Reveal the Ghost tokens of all players. If a player has the most or is tied for the most Ghost tokens they will gain 1 Curse for every 2 Ghost tokens they have (rounded down). 3. Winner The player with the FEWEST Curses wins. If there is a tie, the tied player with the FEWEST Ghost tokens win. If still tied, the players share victory. Cursed cards There are 8 Cursed cards of each type, 2 of each Curse value 1-4. Note: For all card types that dispel cards of their own type the game will automatically dispel the cards with the highest Curse values, as there is no valid reason to select any other cards. Amulet At game end, dispel the Amulet cards indicated by each of your Amulets. Each Amulet card can only dispel 1 Amulet card with the indicated Curse value. Cat At game end, if you have 9 or fewer Ghost tokens, dispel all but 1 Cat card. Clocks If you are the 1st player to collect a set of Clock cards whose Curse values add up to 8 or more, immediately dispel 2 Clock cards. After that, collecting a set of Clock cards has no effect. Doll When you have a set of Doll cards whose Curse values add up to exactly 6, immediately dispel those Doll cards. Holy Water When you collect a set 2 Holy Water cards immediately discard half of your Ghost tokens rounded. Mask When you collect a Mask card, immediately pass 1 Ghost token per mask card in your set to the player on your right. If you have less Ghosts than you are required to pass, pass all possible. Mirror Each time you take a Mirror card, immediately take a Ghost token. When you collect 3 Mirror cards immediately dispel those 3 Mirror cards. Music Box At game end, if you have the most total Curses on Music Box cards, dispel 2 Music Box cards. If tied, all tied players dispel 2 Music Boxes. Portrait At game end, dispel half of your Portrait cards, rounded down. Ring When you collect a set of 4 Ring cards immediately dispel those 4 Ring cards. Tome When you collect a set of 2 Tome Cards, choose a card type (not Tomes) and dispel all the cards of that type. Dispelled cards no longer count as part of a set. Twin When you collect 2 Twin cards with the same Curse value, immediately dispel those 2 Twin cards. Rooms Attic If you place a Meeple on the top space of this Room immediately take a Ghost token. Basement After the dice are rolled for this Room, the player that placed the 3rd Meeple may re-roll ALL of the dice 1 time. Hallway After the dice are rolled for this Room, the player that placed the 3rd Meeple may change 1 die result. Library Place the 3 Cursed cards in this room in left to right in ascending Curse value. The player the takes the leftmost card must first take a Ghost token. The player that takes the rightmost card first discards a Ghost token Nursery If you place a Meeple on the bottom space of this Room immediately discard a Ghost token. Secret Passage Place the 3rd Cursed card in this Room face-down. When a player places a Meeple in the Room they can look at the face-down card. When a 3rd Meeple is placed, reveal the card.

---

community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] I don’t like this game especially if only two of you are playing. It’s highly likely that twins won’t resolve because you don’t know if you’ll be shuffling the complete set of twins in your 2-player deck. And to make matters worse, ghosts only count if you’ve got the most number of ghosts. So if during the game you already have plenty of ghosts, you no longer have a chance to win. Additionally, you can’t eliminate your ghosts if it’s a 2-player game. This game sucks!

[Rating: 2.5/10] complicated rules for a simple game, even when you win you feel like you've lost, unsatisfying

[Rating: 3/10] After Crypt, Canvas and now Don't Go In there, I can simply conclude that R2i can not make a good game despite how many gimmicks they brought into the packaging

[Rating: 3/10] [b]1st Play Thoughts [bgcolor=#FF6699][color=#FF6699]-[/color] [b]3[/b] [color=#FF6699]-[/color][/bgcolor] (Oct 2023):[/b]  I played this digitally on Board Game Arena and did not care for the game at all. It essentially boils down to collecting a bunch of cards you don't want and trying to get the lowest score possible. It didn't really seem to matter what card you got, they were all quite similar and the game seemed fairly random. The artwork was interesting, I sort of liked it but didn't really like it at the same time. The Halloween theme is fun and the game seems to have some pop culture 

[Rating: 3.5/10] Plays pretty awful at 2 player, so yet another game they added the 2 to the box to sucker people in. Can see this being a fine set collection style game for light gamers at higher player counts around Halloween though.  2 player this is a straight - 0 4+ players - 7

[Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  Set collection with ghosts and worker placement of a sort. It was fine but nothing I need to acquire nor play again.

[Rating: 4/10] There are some reasonable ideas here but the game is very underdeveloped and so has lots of issues, e.g. the fact that nothing scales with the number of players. I might go as high as 5 except for the terrible graphic design; I understand they wanted atmosphere but having that at the expense of not being able to read the cards is unacceptable.

[Rating: 4/10] I thought the not wanting to get cards plus the atypical way you draft cards could be interesting, but this game was pretty mediocre for me. Somehow despite what seems like should work on paper didn't lead to a game that felt particularly tense.

[Rating: 4/10] Artwork was not my type when first started playing. However, quite simple game for what it is and some small element of luck. However, you can count and block and hence seems quite fun. Played on BGA. Would play more if theme and artwork was more my style!
